observations:
Torah #124 has zero bechina edges in the dataset and zero bechina-language instances in the source text. Because packages are constructed from bechina (shared-nature/parallel-aspect) relationships only, and none exist for this Torah, no packages of any kind — neither from the dataset nor from gap analysis — can be proposed.

The teaching consists of a single conceptual insight delivered in pure eitza (causal) form: the person's prayer-arguments (cause) → God's pleasure (effect) → God sending enabling words (mechanism) → the person's ability to overcome (outcome). None of these conceptual elements are declared as aspects/parallels of one another — each is a distinct node in a causal chain.

A 'new package' from gap analysis would require finding בְּחִינַת language in the source text that identifies concepts as sharing the same essential nature, where those concepts are absent from the dataset. No such language exists in Torah #124's source text.

The three potential conceptual clusters that could theoretically form packages (prayer/petition, divine pleasure/תענוג, speech/words) are not connected to each other through bechina language — they are connected through causality. Building packages on these connections would violate the fundamental framework rule: packages capture shared nature (bechina), not cause-and-effect chains (eitza).

Conclusion: Torah #124 is a zero-package Torah — a teaching that is entirely causal in its conceptual structure, with no bechina graph.
